newsitem.title: INDIA: India NSE shares finish higher on fund buying.
newsitem.headline: India NSE shares finish higher on fund buying.

text.p: Stray buying in pivotal stocks by foreign institutional investors pushed up share prices at the National Stock Exchange (NSE) on Thursday, traders said.
The 50-stock NSE index closed 11.92 points or 1.16 percent higher at a provisional 1,037.92 after opening at 1,028.66.
Dealers said a holiday at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) led punters to take speculative positions in the market. Some buying by foreign funds also helped share prices record gains.
"The market was pretty strong today with good buying seen in SBI and MTNL," said Rakesh Chandak, dealer at Lloyds Brokerage.
"Some fresh buying is expected in the market."

Traders said the buying was in anticipation of a short rally when the finance bill is passed by parliament next week. The market expects the government to give some tax reliefs to industry and investors to boost sentiment.
"The mood is slightly better," said Rasesh Maniar of Mukesh Babu Securities, a brokerage firm.
SBI, India's largest commercial bank, is expected to begin pre-marketing its $400 million issue of global depositary receipts (GDRs) on September 16, investment bankers said.
"There was definitely some renewed buying in SBI," a dealer said. He added that some fund buying also buoyed the stock."
SBI gained 7.35 rupees to 285.60, Reliance 3 rupees to 211, TISCO 1.75 rupees to 196.25 and ITC 3.25 rupees to 298.80.
The closure of the Bombay and Delhi bourses due to a Hindu religious holiday affected trading volumes, traders said.
They expect the market to stay in positive territory on Friday, when the BSE resumes trade.
"I am bullish. The market should go up," said Lloyds' Chandak.
